title: Handley Page Halifax LW598
memorial_details: Single-stepped rectangular base surmounted by a rectangular sectioned marble pillar incorporating a sloping top face on which is mounted an engraved bronze plaque. At the top of the plaque is a Halifax bomber design with names and inscription below. A single-line border, scalloped at each corner, encloses the aircraft design, names and inscription and all are infilled with white paint. The whole memorial is enclosed by gravel within a kerbed area.
inscription: TO THE MEMORY OF / (6 NAMES) / MEMBERS OF 426 (CANADIAN) SQUADRON FROM LINTON on OUSE / WHO LOST THEIR LIVES IN A HALIFAX BOMBER WHICH CRASHED / NEAR THIS SITE AFTER RETURNING FROM OPERATIONS. / 4.00 a.m. 9th June, 1944. / 'They gave their today for our tomorrow'

sources.title: Facebook post by Paul Goddard (RAF Bomber Command Memorials group) — six crew names and crash time

narrative: Halifax LW598 of 426 (RCAF) Squadron, based at RAF Linton-on-Ouse, crashed near Back Lane, Newton-on-Ouse, North Yorkshire, at approximately 04:00 on 9 June 1944 while returning from operations. All six named crew members were killed. The bronze plaque memorial stands on a marble pillar near the crash site.
cross_reference_note: Two site pages exist for LW598: this record (IWM 29796) and handley-page-halifax-lw598-ow-j-johnnie (IWM 108923). These are two distinct physical memorials at Newton-on-Ouse at nearly identical coordinates. The IWM references differ, confirming they are separate registered memorials. No merge needed — both should be retained.
community_connection: The crew flew from RAF Linton-on-Ouse and came down near Back Lane, Newton-on-Ouse. The village erected the memorial at or near the crash site. Memorial photographed by Paul Goddard.
